answer:
The bastion did not run out of space, and raising its volume would not help.

**Where the error happened.** In job 2817734 the failing task is `ocp4_installer_fetch : Extract the openshift-install binary`, and it failed on `localhost` -- that is, inside the job's execution-environment container on the AAP execution node, extracting into `/tmp/ocp4-installer-t3vkb`. The bastion (`bastion.t3vkb.edge-labs.example.net`) finished its own tasks and reported its root filesystem at 4% used of 200G.

**Where the job runs.** `agd-v2/edge-ai-inference-lab/prod.yaml` pins the item to instance group `exec-pool-b` on west (`bastion_root_volume_size` is already 200).

**What ran out of space.** The controller logs for exec-pool-b show `/var/lib/containers` at 100% used on aap-exec-b02 (0.3 GiB free of 120 GiB) and 99% on aap-exec-b01; each job container's /tmp lives on that volume. exec-pool-a is at 38% and its jobs are succeeding.

**Why.** `podman-image-prune.timer` has been inactive on both exec-pool-b nodes since 2026-09-21T06:00:00Z -- disabled for maintenance MW-4471 and never re-enabled -- so 212 unused EE images have accumulated and filled the volume.

**Impact.** 6 jobs have failed on exec-pool-b since 2026-09-25T00:00:00Z with `[Errno 28] No space left on device`.

**Fix.** Prune images on aap-exec-b01/b02 and re-enable the prune timer; then re-run. The bastion volume change has no effect on this failure and can be dropped.
